encounters.cc: Worsening severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, 10 days after initial pancreatitis diagnosis

lines: Worsening severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, 10 days after initial pancreatitis diagnosis

The patient is a 46-year-old male with severe alcohol use disorder, initially evaluated for alcohol-related symptoms in January 2020, who returns to the emergency department with worsening abdominal pain.
He presents with a 10-day history of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back.
He was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis 7 days ago and was discharged with supportive care.
He now reports that the pain has worsened despite taking prescribed analgesics.
He also complains of nausea and has had several episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting.
- Father with alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis
- Mother with hypertension and major depressive disorder
- One sibling with substance use disorder

Alcohol: Severe alcohol use disorder with physiological dependence; patient reports drinking 'a few beers' nightly but demonstrates withdrawal phenomena (morning tremors, tactile/auditory hallucinations, autonomic hyperactivity) and severe complications including recurrent pancreatitis and malnutrition.
On examination, he is febrile with a temperature of 38.7°C, tachycardic with a heart rate of 112 bpm, and hypotensive with a blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg.
His abdomen is distended, with diffuse tenderness and decreased bowel sounds.
An urgent contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen shows a large area of pancreatic necrosis with gas formation within the collection.
